title: Renewable Energy: Future Power
welcome_lead: From hydrogen to fusion — what powers the next century?
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: future energy, hydrogen, fusion.
final_note: Today's homework helps power tomorrow's world.

concepts.def: Gas that burns with only water as waste.
Device that turns hydrogen into electricity.
Joining atoms to release huge energy.
Network that balances supply and demand.
Energy from rising and falling tides.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hydrogen can be made by splitting water with electricity. Burned or used in a fuel cell, the only waste is water.
Tides are predictable — turbines under the sea make clean power. Wave generators ride the bobbing motion of the sea surface.
Fusion joins small atoms to make bigger ones, releasing energy — like the Sun. Scientists are still trying to make it work on Earth.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Because they generate too much energy.
They are the same problem.
Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).

mcqs.q: Why does renewable energy require energy storage solutions?
options: Because they generate too much energy.
Solar and wind generation are intermittent - storage smooths out supply and demand.
Renewable energy can never meet demand.
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Environmental protection at all costs.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
